observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale. South is a barrel-bodied, wide, tall front view with a large head. East is a slim horizontal theropod profile. North is a narrow rear view. South is clearly the bulkiest and tallest: its legs, head and body are all much wider than on north.
observed.south.png: Front view of a stout upright two-legged reptile. Two small heavy-lidded eyes sit either side of a hooked beak with a deep frown. It has round fleshy cheeks, a pointed crest peak on top of the head and tiny forelimbs held to a pale chest. The thick legs end in clawed toes. The tail emerges from the image-left flank and curves outward and down. The hide is tan with olive net-patterned patches on the flanks and crest.
observed.east.png: True side profile facing right. The horizontal body is balanced over two hind legs, with a long thick tapering tail held straight out behind. It has tiny tucked forelimbs, a blunt beak-like snout, a round cheek pouch, a downturned mouth, one small eye and a backswept crest at the rear of the skull. Olive polygonal patches with tan seams cover the back, the belly is pale tan and the lower legs are reddish-brown.
observed.north.png: Rear view with the back of the crested head, cheek bulges visible on either side, and no eyes or face. The olive-patched back, haunches and two legs are visible, and a thick tail hangs down the centre between the legs. It is much narrower and slighter than south.
observed.scale.png: Beside the human the east view is about waist height or lower, with a body under one cell long. At 32 px per cell it is a faint tan smear with no outline that nearly disappears into the brown ground, while the rat beside it reads sharply.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the face, beak, both eyes, chest and forelimbs toward the camera.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the back of the skull, back, haunches and tail. The side bulges are cheeks, with no eyes or face.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three are standing views with feet on the ground. None is seen from above.

SAME_SIZE.seen: South is a much larger, bulkier animal. Its torso and legs are about 1.4 to 1.5 times as wide as on north and its head is about twice as wide. The measured heights are 175, 116 and 144 px. East being low and long is partly pose, but the south-to-north difference is real.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: Crest, cheeks, beak, forelimbs, tail, palette and net pattern carry across. The south body is fatter and more upright than the slim east body, and its tail swings to one side; noted as polish.

SIGNATURE.seen: The small biped, blunt head, tiny forelimbs and thick balancing tail are all legible on east and south.

ALIEN.seen: It resembles a small theropod or psittacosaur, but this is a canon RSW_ subject whose body plan is stated as dinosaur-like theropod. The beak, jowls and crest keep it from being a named Earth species.

DEPARTURES.seen: 1 bipedal: present on all facings. 2 blunt head: present, rounded beak snout on east and south. 3 tiny forelimbs: present on south and east. 4 thick balancing tail: present on all facings, straight behind on east.

CANON.seen: Body plan: horizontal on east, two legs, tail on every facing. Head: large with blunt beak, cheeks, downturned mouth and backswept crest. Eyes: two modest eyes on south. Colour: tan and olive patches with paler belly and reddish-brown legs; the orange-brown on the back is weak. Size: small. Rendering: realistic scaly skin with no outline. Not a frog and not four-legged.

STYLE.seen: Painterly scaly skin with natural shading and no keyline. The south frown is a little caricatured.

OURS.seen: Reads as original art, and the card lists it as our regeneration output. No vanilla or donor body is recognisable.

ALPHA.seen: Clean edges on all facings, with no ground, shadow or halo on the checkerboard or on brown.

SCALE.seen: East stands well below the human's chest and reads as a small vermin animal, though south at the same scale is noticeably larger.

LEGIBLE.seen: In the 32 px panel it is a faint thin tan and olive smear that merges with brown ground. The rat beside it is far clearer.

reply.subject: RSW_Gizka
reply.image_seen: The facing sheet and individual sprites show a tan-and-olive reptile: a broad frontal animal with a sideways tail, a horizontal biped in profile, and a narrower rear with a central descending tail; the scale panel shows it substantially smaller than the human.

concerns.evidence: At the shared scale, south has substantially bulkier thighs, feet and torso than north. East's horizontal pose explains some of the measured height spread, but does not explain south's enlarged limb thickness and overall mass.

South presents a tall, rounded belly beneath the head, with a tail projecting from the image-left flank and hooking downward. East has an elongated horizontal trunk and rearward balancing tail; north has a central tail. A curved tail alone could be a pose difference, but the frontal torso also changes the animal's build.

The olive reticulated pattern sits over tan hide, with warm brown shading visible on the head's cheeks, lateral torso and thighs, especially in south and east. The belly is paler. Orange is subdued, but the requested warm orange-brown family is represented beyond the lower legs; the hide is not flat-coloured.

South has small recessed eyes, textured cheeks, irregular skin folds and softly modelled shading. The downturned mouth and blunt beak-like snout follow the canon description. The stern expression does not itself establish cartoon rendering.

findings.seen: South has noticeably thicker hind legs, larger feet and a heavier torso than the other facings at the shared scale. Pose accounts for part, but not all, of the flagged 51% height spread.
findings.fix: All facings depict the same body mass, head proportions, hind-leg thickness and foot size at one shared scale.

request.subject: RSW_Gizka

edits.change: All four facings share one body scale: head width, torso width, hind-leg thickness and foot size are identical in south, north, east and west, with the slim build of the east profile as the master. The south view is the same slim animal turned toward the viewer, not a larger or heavier one.

The body is a lean horizontal theropod-style torso held on two hind legs. In the front view (eyes toward the viewer) this torso is foreshortened, seen end-on over the hind legs at the same slim build, with no upright pot belly.

The thick balancing tail grows straight out of the rear pelvis as a continuation of the spine. In the front view it is seen behind the hips, centred on the body line, and it tapers straight back, not hooked sideways from a flank.

Hind legs and feet keep one thickness and one foot size in every facing. The tiny forelimbs stay small and tucked in front of the chest in every facing, and the blunt head keeps one width, about the same as the neck and shoulders plus a little.

invariants: small bipedal reptile standing on two hind legs
one shared scale and slim build across south, north, east and west
painterly vanilla RimWorld style, clean dark outline
request.prompt: A single sprite of a gizka for RimWorld: a small bipedal reptile with a lean, horizontal theropod-style torso balanced on two hind legs. It has a blunt, short-snouted head, tiny forelimbs held close to the chest, and a thick balancing tail growing straight from the rear of the pelvis as a continuation of the spine. Slim build throughout: narrow torso, modest hind legs of even thickness, small feet, and a head only slightly wider than the neck. Muted olive-green scaled skin with a paler belly. Painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, clean dark outline, transparent background. The same animal, at the same size and build, is drawn in every facing. Front view: eyes toward the viewer, the slim torso foreshortened over the hind legs, with the tail visible behind the hips on the body's centre line. Rear view, seen from behind: back, haunches and the thick tail centred on the spine, eyes hidden. Side view: the slim horizontal body with the tail extending straight back as the counterweight. Standing height, hind-leg width and foot size match across all facings.
